title: Practical: String Library
story: You're tired of writing `reverse`, `count_words`, and `capitalize` in every project. Time to build a string toolkit module - organized, tested, and ready to import anywhere.
why: A string utility module centralizes common text operations, making them reusable across programs with a consistent interface.
analogy: A kitchen has a spice rack with labeled jars: 'cinnamon', 'oregano', 'paprika'. Instead of grinding spices fresh every meal, you reach for the jar. A string utility module is your spice rack of text operations.
try_it: Add `to_title_case` that capitalizes the first letter of every word. Add `starts_with(s: Str, prefix: Str)` and `ends_with(s: Str, suffix: Str)`. Write a main function that tests all five functions with various inputs.
tips: Build reverse by iterating backwards through the string
Count words by tracking transitions from space to non-space
Use slice for truncation - it's safe even with out-of-bounds lengths
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle empty strings - always check len() first
Using <= instead of < in loops, causing off-by-one errors
Concatenating strings inefficiently in loops - build once, join at the end
